messages:
Avery: quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime segment. dropping questions + short answers here so we have a single place to reference.

Liam: thanks! first quick one: micro-batching vs wait-for-full-batch tradeoffs 6 what's our recommended default for low-latency chat flows?

Avery: default is conservative: max_batch_delay = 10ms, max_batch_size = 32. our experiments show this keeps p95 latency low while preserving throughput. we'll surface heuristics per route.

Priya: are we going to expose per-route batching knobs in the console or keep it automatic? ops wants a manual override.

Noah: plan is autopilot + override. default = auto-tune, but route-level overrides will be available (UI + API). will document best practices.

Maya: on kernels 5 what's the plan for mixed-precision kernels and fallbacks for rare sequence lengths?

Avery: kernel selector prefers fp16/quantized variant; for extreme seq-lens we fallback to seq-optimized kernel (slower). rollout contains heuristics to prefer stability over micro-gains.

Liam: for Dedicated customers, can they pin to an older kernel if the new one regresses for them?

Avery: yes  we support per-customer pinning to model+kernel artifact. it's a config in the private control plane.

Priya: cache warming is a big concern for bursty jobs. any suggestions for proactive warmup or prefetch?

Noah: we have a warmup API on the roadmap: POST /v1/warmup with prefixes to prime KV and exec caches. ETA: next sprint for Dedicated, later for hosted. meanwhile, customers can send synthetic warmup traffic.

Liam: can we get a short canary policy snippet so SRE can add alerts? (p95, error-rate, batch-rejection-rate)

Avery: snippet below for the rollout controller:

```
rollout:
  phases:
    - pct: 1
      hold: 12h
    - pct: 5
      hold: 24h
    - pct: 30
      hold: 24h
signals:
  latency:
    p95_threshold_multiplier: 1.2
  errors:
    absolute_increase_pct: 100
  batching:
    rejected_rate_threshold: 0.05
```

Priya: nice. can we also track batch-size median and 99th? helps tune max_batch_size.

Avery: added to the telemetry plan.

Noah: docs question: what should we put in the release notes for customers when we flip the adaptive batching or kernel autotune flags? short, non-technical blurb + link to deep-dive.

Maya: suggested blurb: "Improved serving runtime: adaptive batching and kernel autotune to reduce latency and cost. No action required; opt-out available via route settings. See docs for details." Keep it 1 line.

Liam: who owns the deep-dive doc? I can take the batching section if Priya takes kernel behavior.

Priya: I'll own kernel + telemetry. Liam and I will co-edit. target draft in 5 business days.

DeployBot: rollout-controller: created experiment runtime/kernel-autotune-v1 at 1782005205 :rocket:

Avery: thanks, team. I'll post a short summary to the release thread and link the doc drafts once they're up. if anyone sees odd telemetry after the rollout starts, ping here with screenshots. :eyes:
